title: Coherent sheaves with zero-dimensional support are acyclic and generated
statement:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Suppose its support, the set of points with nonzero stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], has topological Krull dimension at most zero [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then $\mathcal F$ is generated by its global sections, that is, the evaluation map $\bigoplus_{s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal F$ is surjective, and
$$H^i(X,\mathcal F)=0\quad\text{for every }i>0.$$
In particular $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)=0$ implies $\mathcal F=0$. Cohomology is Zariski module-sheaf cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 0B3J, lemma-coherent-support-dimension-0 (both conclusions, and the immediate zero-section consequence).

proof.text: By [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent of finite type. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-support]: its annihilator cuts out a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $i(Z)=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$, and its ideal annihilates $\mathcal F$. The closed-immersion definition identifies $|Z|$ homeomorphically with this support, so $\dim Z\leq0$.

source.place: Tag 0B3J, first sentence; Tag 01Y5 and Morphisms Tags 05JU, 05JV

proof.text: The immersion $i$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft](2), so [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $Z$ locally Noetherian. The coherent equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence](1), applied to the annihilating ideal from step 1, gives a coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal F\cong i_*\mathcal G$. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-noetherian-zero-dimensional-discrete] to $Z$: every subset of $Z$ is open.

For $z\in Z$, the open singleton $\{z\}$ is the smallest neighbourhood of $z$, hence $\mathcal G_z=\mathcal G(\{z\})$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Any $t\in\mathcal G_z$ extends to $Z$ by gluing $t$ on $\{z\}$ with zero on $Z\setminus\{z\}$, whose overlap is empty. This gives a global section of $\mathcal F=i_*\mathcal G$ with prescribed germ at $i(z)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks]; stalks off $i(Z)$ are zero by the same node. Thus every stalk element is the germ of a global section. Locally that germ agrees with its chosen representative, so the evaluation map in the statement is locally surjective (the coefficient of the chosen section is $1$), and hence is a surjective sheaf map.

source.place: Tag 0B3J, global-generation conclusion, expanding the disjoint-union argument

proof.text: For opens $U\subseteq V\subseteq X$, both $i^{-1}U$ and its complement in $i^{-1}V$ are open in the discrete space $Z$. A section in $\mathcal F(U)=\mathcal G(i^{-1}U)$ extends by gluing with zero on that complement to $\mathcal G(i^{-1}V)=\mathcal F(V)$. The overlap is empty, so the sheaf axiom applies without any finiteness assumption. Every restriction map of the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal F$ is therefore surjective: it is flasque in the precise sense of [def-sc-zariski-flasque].

source.place: Tag 0B3J, disjoint-union-of-affines reduction; zero extension spells out flasqueness

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-module-cup-flasque-acyclicity] to this module sheaf on $X$. It gives $H^i(X,\mathcal F)=0$ for each natural $i>0$, for module-sheaf cohomology as required.

source.place: Tag 09SY, lemma-flasque-acyclic; applied to the flasque module from step 4

proof.text: If $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)=0$, step 3 says every stalk element is zero. For any section on any open, each germ is then zero, hence it vanishes on a neighbourhood of each point by [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. These neighbourhoods cover the open, so sheaf uniqueness makes the section zero. Thus $\mathcal F=0$. For empty support this argument already gives $\mathcal F=0$; no nonempty or finite-support assumption entered.

source.place: Tag 0B3J, immediate consequence of global generation
